text: A horse can outrun Orcs, Trolls, even Giants. Not arrows. Or Doom Divers. But it still helps.
Can't be properly imposing without a plated barding for the horse.

During the Siege of Remas, a cannonball flew straight at Borgio. Instead of rather influential smithereens, bystanders witnessed that the projectile was stuck right into the Prince's armour, who was barely wounded. Melted and reshaped as a mace, the cannonball makes for a terrifying and symbolic weapon.
During the most furious melees, Borgio wears his frightening mask, a grotesque grimace of malice. Coupled with the wearer's bulk and might, the effect is scary indeed.
Only some scholars might know what those statues were about, but once melted and used to forge this huge brazen armour, they might have brought over whatever enchantment they used to bear...
Knowledge is power, and this learning comes from the Strigoi patriarch's secrets and mistakes.
One of Ushoran's own artefacts, this polestaff supposedly allowed the original Strigoi patriarch to hold off the Lahmians' aggression for so long.

A proper Bretonnian steed, fast and with fine cloth barding. None of that spiky steely business.
Lucrezzia always wears, somewhere on her person, a dagger coated with another of her brews. Can't blame someone for being prepared for a midnight stab.

Good metal barding is important against foes that can otherwise cleave your horse in twain in one blow.
A rare arabyan Pegasus, gifted by Crusaders. A living and swift siphon of light and magic, ready to unleash their energy on aggressors.
A Dwarf's grudge is forever, but so is his gratitude for many lives saved. The unexpected gift of a family runic axe is to be remembered for just as long.

Formerly a magic and fluttering arabyan turban, this souvenir bears energetic enchantments. The cadre of Myrmidian priests who prodded it for a week have testified that the scarf won't strangle Gausser of its own initiative anytime soon, which is oddly specific.

I had actually sent to buy a unicorn. Made of diamonds. Like, a real live unicorn made of diamonds, very stylish. But they say it can't be done. Unimaginative buggers, the lot of them.
Lupio's own demigryph owes his companionship to Lupio and "Big Magpie" nickname to his distinctive black and white coat and attraction towards shiny baubles.
An ancient elven blade, relic of a time when Tilea was an Asur colony. Its wielder's attacks leave a glowing and elegant trail of light and molten armour.
Catrazza is not usually one for religious displays, but there are solid practical and diplomatical advantages for wearing this ring around.
A cloak made of Lustrian gold, with uncertain magic properties. Its known feature is to give Lupio immense satisfaction.
Reaped during a confusing skirmish against reptiles, elf corsairs and marauders, this ring bears an eerie and intriguing aura over it. Inquisitors never managed to get it off Lupio for investigation.
Cadavo's current steed is an ill-tempered gelding only loyal and tending to Cadavo. To those few he doesn't kick on sight, he answers to the name of Broccolo.

An amulet made of a weird alloy, capable of neutralizing poisons and many of the magical properties for weapons that would injure the bearer.

A lucky prey from a skirmish against Corsairs, this rare magical repeater crossbow is too cumbersome for use on foot, but if you want something positively dead, it's a nice toy. Just have to hope the magic in it isn't too dark.
This baby can do zero to fifty in nothing! And I swear she can understand everything I- did she just write sixty" with her hoof?"
A reward from the Slann, this amulet in the shape of Sotek's tongue feels oddly alive and protected the wearer more times than he recalls.
Used by someone to write an otherwise uninteresting map, this scroll bears potent enchantments of Nehekharan protective magic. However, it tends to crumble a bit with each use.
Some people mistake Lupio's battlefield antics for astute shows of force and bravery for the troops. Truth is, they're Lupio's own satisfaction.

The weapon is an old gift from the Black Guard to the then-High Eagle of Myrmidia, and later made its way to Eustaquio. It is excruciatingly sharp and smells faintly of rotting roses. No matter what, Eustaquio seems to be viciously gripping it like a life-line.
The best smiths were called to restore Eustaquio's plate armour. However, he wouldn't let anyone replace the chest piece or repair the hole through which the Nehekharans ripped out his heart.
This ancient shield might predate the city of Luccini, and still embodies the power of the sun.
This blade is believed to be the actual sword used by his remote ancestor, Lucan, one of the twin divine founders of Luccini.
A ring bearing the cameo of Luccina, sorceress and sister of Lucan. This enchanted item sings inspiring hymns and exhortations that embolden nearby troops.
Like his predecessor, Piggolo II doesn't crave the battlefield. But when hand-to-hand combat is required, or rather tusk-to-groin, he is clad in a custom panoply proper for his status and girth.
The chest wagon is Piggolo's most customary campaigning mount.
The re-experimental tank is Piggolo's ultimate battle mount, from within which his tactical acumen can dominate the battlefield.
